newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-BRILLIANT RONALDO LIFTS BARCELONA CLEAR IN SPAIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BRILLIANT RONALDO LIFTS BARCELONA CLEAR IN SPAIN.

text.p: Another scintillating performance from Brazilian striker Ronaldo gave Barcelona a 5-1 win at Compostela and with it the lead in the Spanish first division on Saturday.

Ronaldo scored two superb goals, one of them after picking up the ball in his own half, and set up two more as Bobby Robson's side opened up a three-point lead over Real Betis ahead of Sunday's games.
Betis scored late to earn a 2-2 draw at Atletico Madrid and move ahead of Real Madrid, who play Racing Santander on Sunday.
Barcelona's game was less than 40 seconds old when Ronaldo broke down the right and his cross found the back of the net after hitting a Compostela defender.

Shortly afterwards Ronaldo hit the post after slipping clear, and on the quarter hour he appeared on the left, swerved beautifully past Mauro Garcia and found fellow Brazilian Giovanni, who had no problems making it 2-0.
But the best was still to come.

With 10 minutes left in the first half, Ronaldo robbed a ball from two Compostela men, crossed the half-way line, skipped through three more challenges and blasted the ball past keeper Fernando Peralta.
Right after the break it was Ronaldo again, as the Brazilian picked up a ball from Luis Figo and burst ahead of two defenders to score his second.
Figo added another for Barcelona after a mistake by Peralta before Nigerian international Christopher Ohen pulled one back for Compostela with a brave diving header.
The match ended with a standing ovation for Ronaldo from the Compostela fans.
"Ronaldo could be the latest Di Stefano or Pele," said Compostela manager Fernando Vazquez afterwards.
Another visiting player who earned the applause of home fans was Gabriel Moya, who led Valencia to a 2-0 victory at his old club Sevilla.
Moya led the Valencia attack in the absence of Brazilian striker Romario, dropped by coach Luis Aragones.

The victory lifted Valencia to a mid-table position and relieved the pressure on Aragones. But the result increased the tension surrounding another well-known name in Spanish football, Sevilla manager Jose Antonio Camacho.
While Sevilla languish third from bottom, local rivals Real Betis continued their good start to the season by earning a point at champions Atletico.

International striker Alfonso Perez had put the southerners ahead before mistakes at corners let Juan Carlos Gomez and Argentine midfielder Diego Simeone through to leave Atletico 2-1 ahead at the break.
But with just four minutes on the clock, Juan Sabas clinched the equaliser that put Betis in second place.
UEFA Cup sides Espanyol and Tenerife both slipped up ahead of midweek continental action.
Espanyol could manage only a goalless draw at home to Celta Vigo while Tenerife crashed 3-1 to Valladolid.

Zaragoza fans armed with 15,000 whistles gave the referee for their match with Athletic Bilbao a noisy reception in a protest against a penalty decision in their last home game against Barcelona. But the game went off without incident and ended 1-1.
